item.title: Radio Kerry and Fexco ask public to nominate Kerry Heroes 2025
item.description: Radio Kerry and Fexco are asking people to nominate who they consider to be the Kerry Heroes of 2025. item.title: 22 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry
item.description: There are 22 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry today. That’s according to figures from the Irish Nurses' and Midwives' Organisation. There are 17 patients waiting on trolleys in UHK’s ED today, while a further five people are on trolleys in wards in the hospital. Advertisement Nationally, there are 524 people waiting for a bed in hospitals today. University Hospital Limerick is the worst affected by overcrowding with 85 people waiting on trolleys there.

item.title: HSE confirms opening of additional beds at West Kerry Community Hospital
item.description: The HSE has confirmed that additional beds have opened at the West Kerry Community Hospital. Two beds opened at Ospidéal Pobail Corca Dhuibhne on Monday, with a further two beds expected to open in the coming week. In a statement to Radio Kerry, the HSE South West says there is no confirmed timeline for the opening of additional beds in Kenmare Community Nursing Unit. item.title: Castleisland business makes €4 million investment in renewable energy project
item.description: A Castleisland business has made a €4 million investment in a renewable energy project which will see their carbon emissions reduce by 95%. Tony Walsh of Walsh Colour Print and Educate.ie says the investment makes sense as it will cut their emissions and energy bills. item.title: Kerry TD calls for state agencies to come together and ensure St Finan’s landbank isn’t sold to developers
item.description: A Kerry TD has said state bodies need to come together and ensure the St Finan’s landbank in Killarney is not sold to private developers. The HSE-owned, former mental health hospital, closed in 2012 and has lain idle since. The Land Development Agency has formally expressed an interest in acquiring half of the 13.2-hectare site, but not the hospital building itself as it’s not suitable for conversion to residential use. item.description: Amnesty International says the charges against a Kerry man are baseless and must be dropped. item.title: High Court grants Revenue order against Nathan McDonnell
item.description: A Kerry businessman who was jailed for 12 years for the importation of crystal meth faces having part of the proceeds of the sale of his family home being forfeit to the Revenue Commissioners. The Irish Independent reports that the High Court has granted Revenue an order appointing a receiver over 50 per cent of the net proceeds of the sale of the house owned by Nathan McDonnell. The house at Clashaphuca, Ballyroe, Tralee is 50% owned by Nathan McDonnell and his wife Jackie owns the other half.

item.title: Crime re-offending rate in Kerry was above national average in 2024
item.description: The crime re-offending rate in Kerry last year was above the national average. That’s according to the latest figures from the Central Statistics Office. It shows over 4,400 (4,433) incidents were detected on the Garda pulse system in Kerry in 2024. Advertisement Of these 63% (2,773) were linked to a suspected offender who had at least one previous detection. Nationally, 61% of crimes were linked to re-offenders; while theft incidents accounted for the highest suspect re-offences. Advertisement
